reason: This Exodus 12 passage describes both the regular people (בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל) and their leaders (Moses and Aaron) as obedient and unified in following God's commands. The text explicitly states 'And all the children of Israel did as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron' (וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֖וּ כָּל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽת־ אַהֲרֹ֖ן). There is no moral judgment distinguishing the people as 'wrong' while the leaders are 'right.' Instead, the narrative portrays a coordinated exodus where both leaders and people demonstrate compliance with divine instruction. The story's focus is on God's deliverance rather than on any fault or righteousness disparity between the people and their leaders.
